findings.issue: At 1440 px the intro's running text runs about 790 px wide, about 95 characters a line ("Production and export sit within one company, so quality, cost and delivery stay under our direct"; the shortest sample is the same width), well past the 70ch measure treatment-practice sets and past the audit's 80ch limit.
findings.reference: The competitor's intro/proof paragraphs sit in their own text column; treatment.md fixes running text at 17/25.5 held to 70ch, so our measure follows our own rule, not the competitor's even wider 1440 lines.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, give the intro block's paragraphs (.block--intro p, or its text column) max-width: 70ch so the lines wrap at about 70 characters; leave the heading's width and the fit sizing alone.

findings.issue: The step numbers are still the browser's default list numbers ("1.", "2." … "6.") in body size and body colour (patterns.css .point-list__item::marker is var(--text-primary)), so the six steps read as a plain ordered text list rather than a process.
findings.reference: The competitor marks each step with a large, accent-blue, zero-padded numeral ("01", "02", "03") in its own column beside the step title.
findings.fix: In reference.css, scope to .block--process: set .point-list__items to list-style: none with a counter, and give each .point-list__item a ::before of counter(step, decimal-leading-zero) in color: var(--accent-text), font-weight: 700, about twice the body size, set in a grid column of its own beside the title and text. As a lighter alternative, style ::marker with the accent colour, weight 700 and a larger size, and widen .point-list__items padding-left to fit.

findings.issue: The step titles ("Scale and trial print", "A4 approval options", …) are still the same weight and nearly the same size as their descriptions, so each step's name does not stand out from its text.
findings.reference: The competitor sets each step name ("Custom Designs", "Ready Designs", "Mix n' Match") bold and a little larger than its body text, with a small gap before the description.
findings.fix: In reference.css, give .block--process .point-list__title font-weight: 700, font-size: var(--size-subheading) (1.0625rem is already set on .block--process) and margin-bottom: 0.5rem.

findings.issue: The section still has no heading: its only intro, "Quality checks at every stage of an order", is a lead at body size, so the left column looks almost empty and the section has no title next to m7's H2.
findings.reference: The competitor's process list always opens with an H2 ("3 Ways to Handover") above its lead.
findings.fix: Site Factory should supply a heading for overview-steps (for example "Quality Checks at Every Stage") so the block renders an h2.process__heading above the lead.

findings.issue: The steps still run on with only white space between them, so in the long six-step sample each step blurs into the next.
findings.reference: The competitor separates its steps with thin, light horizontal rules, with even padding above and below each one.
findings.fix: In reference.css, give .block--process .point-list__item border-top: 1px solid var(--border-color) and padding-top equal to the list gap (and border-bottom on :last-child), keeping the 1rem gap from .point-list__items.

findings.issue: At 1440 px the step descriptions run about 90 characters a line ("We send you digital mock-ups so you can approve the scale, and we turn strike-offs around in"), above the 80ch limit for running text.
findings.reference: The competitor's step text keeps to roughly 65–75 characters a line in its right column.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set max-width: 70ch on .block--process .point-list__item p, so the text holds to the measure without fixing the column's width.

findings.issue: On phones, a band of about 70 px separates the one-line lead "Quality checks at every stage of an order" from the first step, much more than the gap between steps, so the lead reads as cut off from its list.
findings.reference: The competitor's process module stacks its intro and steps with gaps close to its row spacing, without an empty band between them.
findings.fix: In reference.css, under the stacked (single-column) breakpoint, reduce the row-gap between the process intro column and .point-list__items in .block--process to about the list's own 1–1.5rem gap.

findings.issue: The check-list item titles (e.g. 'Production Standards', 'Certificate Copies') are set in a light 400 weight, barely heavier than the description under them, so the list has no clear sub-heading level under the bold 700 H2.
findings.reference: The competitor sets every sub-heading under an h2 bold (card h3 Maison 700, accordion questions 700, h4 24px), so each item reads as a heading over its text.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css give the iconList item title (the iconList item heading / h3 selector) font-weight: 700 (or 600 at least), leaving its size to the template.

findings.issue: On phones the item titles that wrap ('Fabric-specific / Certification', 'Shipment-level / Recycled Claims', 'Buyer-appointed / Factory Audits' in m3, same treatment in m7) use body-like leading of about 1.5, so their two lines drift apart and read as two separate lines rather than one heading.
findings.reference: The competitor's multi-line headings sit at about 1.4 leading or tighter (h2 60/84, FAQ summary 1.4), and its card titles stay compact.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css set line-height: 1.2–1.25 on the iconList item title, alongside the weight change for m3.

findings.issue: The check marks are thin, pale aqua strokes that nearly vanish on white at both widths, so the list's icon barely registers as a marker.
findings.reference: On light backgrounds the competitor uses its deep blue #1670a8 for accents (eyebrows, links); it keeps aqua for filled shapes such as its button, not for thin strokes on white.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css colour the iconList check icon with the darker accent (var(--accent-text) / #1670a8), or thicken its stroke so it reaches 3:1 against white.

findings.issue: Each card's number stands on a line of its own above the title, with a full line of space under it. This adds a whole row to every card's head (on phones the number plus a two-line title take about 110px before the text starts) and reads as a separate label rather than part of the title.
findings.reference: The competitor sets the number inline in the bold title, as one line ('01. Custom Designs'), and the text follows straight under it (section-modules.json home 7).
findings.fix: In FeatureGridBlock.astro, for the outline-numbered pattern, render the number inside .feature-card__title as an inline prefix ('01. ') in the title's own type, and drop the card's separate number row from the subgrid (cardRows). The 'numbered' pattern keeps its large number on top.

findings.issue: The gap between a card's title and its text is tight, about 20px at 1440 against the competitor's roughly 40px, so the title sits close on the paragraph. This shows in both samples.
findings.reference: The competitor leaves a clear band of space under each card title before the text, about one and a half body lines.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, add margin-block-end of about 1.25rem to [data-pattern="outline-numbered"] .feature-card__title (or a matching row-gap on the card's subgrid).

findings.issue: On desktop, the body paragraphs run the full width of the copy column at a small size, so lines reach about 80–87 characters (e.g. 'That cuts your development cost and your fit risk for a first collection. You can build'); splitMedia-2 does the same ('Order one before you decide between screen printing, heat transfers, embroidery or'). That is above the treatment practice's 70ch measure and its 80ch audit limit.
findings.reference: The competitor's split copy keeps its paragraphs to a narrower column, at roughly 70–75 characters per line beside the media.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, give the splitMedia copy's paragraphs a max-width of about 68ch, or raise the split copy's body font-size on desktop to the mobile size, so lines stay under 70ch. Keep the copy column's edge shared with the photo, and leave the heading's size to the template's fit.

findings.issue: The figure column is stretched to the copy's height like a photo, so the first panel (Sample fee / Design fee bars) grows to about twice its content and its lower half is an empty blush box.
findings.reference: The competitor's media in this module (the sampling video) keeps its own proportions next to the copy and has no padding or empty area; its blush 'Our Swimwear Sampling Studio' panel is only as tall as its content.
findings.fix: In the split component, apply the 'stretch to the copy's height' rule to photos only: give .split__media panels that hold figures/charts grid-auto-rows: min-content (or align-self: start on each panel), so each panel fits its content and the stack sits at the top of the column, or level with the copy's middle when the copy is longer.

findings.issue: The first paragraph is set as a lead, about 20px on phones and about 19px on desktop, so it is a full step larger than the paragraphs under it (and larger than the single paragraph in 'related'). On a phone it runs five big lines before the body text starts.
findings.reference: The competitor's split module sets every paragraph at one body size ('From seamless bikinis…' matches the text under it) and marks key points in bold, not with a bigger first paragraph.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, set .block--split { --size-lead: var(--size-body); } (or style .block--split .block__lead with font-size: inherit), so the first paragraph of a split row matches the body text.

findings.issue: Two brand names ('NORTHFOLD BASICS', 'HARBOUR KNIT CO.') wrap to two lines inside the 10rem items while the other four stay on one, and because items are centred vertically the names and their 'Swimwear, …' notes sit at different heights across the one row.
findings.reference: The competitor's marks sit on one shared line across the row, each a single mark of even height with nothing wrapping.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css set --logos-item-width so the longest name keeps to one line (sized from our copy, not a fixed copy of the competitor), or top-align the items in .logos-marquee__row (align-items: start) so names and notes share their lines.

findings.issue: All six items fit, so the marquee stays still and the row is packed to the left, leaving the right quarter of the content column as an empty band beside it.
findings.reference: The competitor's logo row runs the full width of the page and off its right edge, the marks spaced evenly across it.
findings.fix: Widen --logos-gap in src/styles/reference.css so the still row reaches the content's right edge (or lets the marquee run when it no longer fits), rather than leaving the items gathered on the left.

findings.issue: In the longest sample the heading 'What buyers say' is drawn in a light, regular-looking weight, while the same heading in the shortest sample is bold. The same mismatch shows on mobile, so the one module renders its h2 in two weights.
findings.reference: The competitor's testimonials heading ('What Independent Labels Say') is set bold (Maison 700), like every one of its section headings.
findings.fix: Find why the first testimonials block on the board does not get the 700 weight that `.block h2 { font-weight: var(--weight-heading) }` (template.css:209) gives it, which the manifest reports as 700. Look for a later rule, or the heading-fit code, that overrides the weight on that instance (`.testimonials__heading`), so that every testimonials h2 renders at --weight-heading.

findings.issue: This repeats the earlier finding, which has not been repaired. The quote cards are still flat white panels with no shadow, so they lack the competitor's raised-card look.
findings.reference: The competitor's quote cards sit on the sage band with a soft drop shadow along the bottom and right edges, which lifts each card off the band.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, give .block--testimonials a soft --shadow-card (e.g. 0 6px 12px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.15)) so that .testimonial picks it up through box-shadow: var(--shadow-card).

findings.issue: This repeats the earlier finding, which has not been repaired. A hard black 1px rule still runs across every card between the quote and the attribution, at both widths.
findings.reference: The competitor's cards separate the quote from the bold name with space only, with no rule.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, set `.block--testimonials .testimonial figcaption { border-top: 0; }` and keep the existing padding-top/gap as the separation.

findings.issue: This repeats the earlier finding, which has not been repaired. reference.css:268 still paints this one section's background (`.block--testimonials { background: var(--surface-band-mint) }`) instead of tinting through --section-tint. The template's white/tinted alternation therefore does not control it: on the board, the logos section above is white, and on a page it can land beside another tinted section.
findings.reference: The competitor's testimonials sit on a sage #d6e2de band. Under the site's rule that sage is the shared section tint, not a colour fixed on one module.
findings.fix: Remove the background rule on .block--testimonials (reference.css:268) and set --section-tint to the sage (#d6e2de) in the treatment, so that the template's alternation decides which sections carry it.

findings.issue: This repeats the earlier finding, which has not been repaired. With two testimonials, the carousel keeps three-card widths and leaves the right third of the row as an empty sage gap.
findings.reference: The competitor's row is always filled by the cards in view, so it has no empty slot. The number of cards in view should follow our own item count, not a fixed 3.
findings.fix: Have the testimonials carousel set its cards-per-view (data-columns) from the item count when every item fits (2 items → 2 columns), or centre a short single row, as the card-set rule does for a short last row.

findings.issue: With a single related page (shortest sample, "Bikinis") the grid's column count is set to the link count (RelatedLinks.astro: count <= 4 ? count), so the one card fills the whole ~1300px content width: one short word on the left edge and its arrow ~1250px away on the right, reading as an empty bar rather than a link card.
findings.reference: The competitor's links and buttons are sized to their label (black 8px-radius title-case buttons and arrow links on the manufacturer page), never a lone full-width bar; in our own longest sample each card takes a third of the row.
findings.fix: In template.css, give .related-pages--grid .related-links a column-width cap, e.g. grid-template-columns: repeat(var(--related-columns, 3), minmax(0, min(100%, 24rem))) at >=600px and >=900px, or set the column floor to 3 in RelatedLinks.astro (columns = max(columns, 3) for counts under 3). The cards then keep one card width and start on the content's left edge.

findings.issue: Our two-column FAQ puts the heading in a narrow left column with the questions in one column to its right. On the longest sample this squeezes 'Frequently Asked Questions' into three one-word lines, while the competitor's module is built differently.
findings.reference: The competitor's FAQ (home 16) puts its eyebrow and heading across the full content width on one line. Under them the questions split into two side-by-side columns of hairline rows, each with a + at its right.
findings.fix: Give the faq two-column variant an arrangement with the heading across the top, starting on the content's left edge. Set the .faq__items below it as a two-column grid of rows, letting the column count follow the question length (one column when the questions are too long for two). Today the heading sits beside the list.

findings.issue: On the shortest sample the questions wrap after about 60% of their row. A blank gap of about 350 px opens between each question's text and its + at the right edge, and the same short lines show on mobile.
findings.reference: The competitor's questions run from the row's left edge to just before the +, so each row reads as one line ending in its mark.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css, remove the max-width / measure cap (and any text-wrap: balance) from .block--faq:is([data-variant="two-column"], [data-variant="accordion"]) .faq__item h3 so the question fills the summary up to the ::after mark.

findings.issue: The question list has rules only under each row. Its first question floats with no line above it, so the list's top edge is undefined next to the heading.
findings.reference: The competitor draws a hairline above the first row as well, under the heading, so every question sits between two rules.
findings.fix: Add border-top: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--text-primary) 18%, transparent) to .block--faq[data-variant="two-column"] .faq__items (or to its first .faq__item), matching the rules between rows.

findings.issue: On phones the questions wrap well short of the column. For example, 'Can you show examples of swimwear / you've made for brands selling / in Europe or North America?' leaves about 70 px of each 350 px row empty, so the rows grow to three or four lines with ragged short lines.
findings.reference: The competitor's questions run the full row width up to the + mark.
findings.fix: Let .block--faq .faq__item h3 fill the summary width up to the mark on phones: no max-width and no text-wrap: balance. Keep the 15px bold navy type.

findings.issue: The band's button is a transparent pill with a thin white outline (`[data-variant="image-band"] .cta .button--primary { background: transparent; border: 1px solid currentColor }`), but in the competitor shot its buttons are solid white pills with dark labels, so ours is the weakest thing on the dark band rather than the clear action.
findings.reference: Competitor home 17: BOOK A CALL-BACK, WHATSAPP, VISIT US and EMAIL US are filled white pills with black uppercase labels sitting on the darkened photo. components.md item 13 calls them white-outlined, but the captured state shows them filled.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set `[data-variant="image-band"] .cta .button--primary` to `background: var(--text-inverse); color: #000000; border-color: var(--text-inverse)` and use the current outline look as its :hover state. Keep the border radius and size as they are.

findings.issue: On the longest sample, the button label 'TALK TO US ABOUT SWIMWEAR PACKAGING & CUSTOM BRAND LABELS' wraps to three centred lines, which turns the pill into a tall stadium shape that is almost as heavy as the paragraph above it.
findings.reference: The competitor's band buttons carry one to three words (BOOK A CALL-BACK, WHATSAPP, VISIT US, EMAIL US), so each stays a one-line pill even on phones.
findings.fix: Shorten the CTA button label in Site Factory to a few words, for example 'Request a label quote', and leave the full topic to the heading.

findings.issue: At both widths the photo band sits inside the content gutter, about 20 px in from the screen edge on both sides. It reads as a boxed panel rather than a full-width photo band, which shows most on phones, where it lines up with the FAQ list above it.
findings.reference: The competitor's image band on home 17 runs edge to edge of the viewport at 1440 px and at 390 px, with no side margin.
findings.fix: Let `.block--cta[data-variant="image-band"]` break out of the container: `margin-inline: calc(50% - 50vw)` with `width: 100vw` on the `.cta` frame, or use the template's full-bleed band setting if it has one. Keep the copy's inline padding so the text stays on the content's left edge.

findings.issue: The section heading "Rash Guard Fabrics, UPF Ratings and Certifications" still renders in a light/regular weight while the card titles under it are bold, so the h2 reads weaker than its own h3s.
findings.reference: The competitor's card-section heading ("Selecting Colours and adding Digital Prints") is a heavy bold sans, clearly stronger than its bold but smaller card titles.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css give the featureGrid section heading the site's heading weight (e.g. .block--featureGrid h2 { font-weight: var(--weight-heading); }, 700), leaving its fitted size to the template.

findings.issue: On phones the light section heading sits over card titles that are about as large and much bolder ("Performance fabric range", "Repeated board contact"), so the step from h2 to card title is lost.
findings.reference: The competitor's mobile heading is bold and clearly outranks its card titles.
findings.fix: The same rule as on desktop (font-weight: var(--weight-heading) on the featureGrid h2) at every width; no size change.

findings.issue: The four cards are still white boxes with a 1px black outline (--border-color #000000), which gives the grid a wireframe look on the white section.
findings.reference: The competitor's card modules for this page type (solution sections 2 and 7) are flat filled panels (white or cream on a tinted band, cream or light blue on navy) with a small radius and no outline.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css set the featureGrid:cards cards (.feature-card in the cards variant) to border-color: transparent with a tinted fill (background: var(--surface-secondary), or white when the section itself is tinted), keeping --radius-card.

findings.issue: The two wide cards use the same thin black outline on white, so the short set reads as two mostly empty framed boxes.
findings.reference: The competitor's two-card row ("Choose from 100,000 m in stock" / "Digital prints") is made of filled rounded panels without borders.
findings.fix: The same card rule as m2: no border on the featureGrid:cards cards, a tinted fill instead.

findings.issue: The card title is still hyphenated inside a word ("Pool and train- / ing performance").
findings.reference: The competitor's card titles wrap only between words.
findings.fix: Set hyphens: manual and overflow-wrap: normal on .feature-card__title in src/styles/reference.css so titles break at spaces only.

findings.issue: The four stacked outlined cards sit about 30px apart, each in its own frame, so they read as a long run of separate boxes instead of one grouped set.
findings.reference: The competitor's stacked mobile cards are filled panels with tight, even gaps on the section's band.
findings.fix: Once the outline is replaced by a fill, reduce the mobile row-gap of the featureGrid:cards grid to the site's smaller spacing step (e.g. 1rem).

findings.issue: Each point's title (e.g. 'Regenerated Fibre Performance', 'Requested Fabrics And Trade-offs') is still set in regular weight and is smaller than the paragraph under it, so the 8-item list reads as one undifferentiated run of text with the hierarchy inverted (same on desktop and in featureGrid-6).
findings.reference: The competitor sets sub-heads under a section heading in its bold heading face (700, at or above the 16-17px body), so each item's title can be scanned on its own.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css give .point-list__title the display face at weight 700 and a size at least equal to the item text (e.g. font-family: var(--font-display); font-weight: 700; font-size: 1.0625rem), keeping its small gap to the paragraph.

findings.issue: This sample's heading 'Ready-to-Brand Curvy Collections and Low-MOQ Trend Drops' is set in a light/regular weight, while the same module's heading in m2 ('Recycled Fabrics and Low-Impact Production') is bold 700, so one module shows two heading weights depending on its copy (also on mobile).
findings.reference: The competitor keeps one heading weight per level (its h2s are always the bold heading face); only the size may follow the words.
findings.fix: In the bullets module's heading CSS (patterns.css, .feature-grid__heading / .point-list__intro h2), set font-weight to the h2 weight (700) independently of the fit step, so the fitting only changes font-size and never the weight.

findings.issue: With only two points the list still runs one column across the whole right track, so its lines run about 90-95 characters ('Our low-MOQ, ready-to-brand trend drops let you test what sells in your market before you'); the 70ch cap in reference.css does not reach these item paragraphs.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps body copy beside a heading to short lines of about 60-75 characters.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css extend the reading-column cap to the point items (e.g. .point-list__item p { max-inline-size: 70ch; }), not only to main[data-authoring-page] .block p, so the measure holds on every page whatever the item count.

findings.issue: The points are still marked with the browser's default small black disc bullets, which look generic and match nothing else in the treatment (same in featureGrid-6 and on mobile).
findings.reference: The competitor's lists (e.g. 'Every price includes' in its pricing panel) mark items with check icons in its accent colour.
findings.fix: In src/styles/reference.css restyle [data-pattern="bullets"] .point-list__item markers (::marker color/content, or list-style: none plus an accent check mask as iconList:checks uses) so they follow the competitor's check-list style.

findings.issue: At 390 px the label column takes about 45% of the table, so the text column is squeezed to roughly 20 characters a line and each row runs 10–15 lines (Certifications, Fabrics, Design and samples), turning the table into a long narrow strip of broken text.
findings.reference: The competitor's text on phones runs the full content width in comfortable 35–45 character lines (body 16px/26px); no section of theirs packs prose into a column this narrow.
findings.fix: In reference.css at max-width 600px, stack a two-column .table-block[data-variant="grid"]: tr display:block with its border-bottom, th/td display:block, first cell set as a small bold label over the full-width text cell (thead visually hidden). Otherwise narrow the first column (th:first-child, td:first-child inline-size: min-content / ~30%) so the text column gets the width.

findings.issue: The four-column size table runs past the right edge on phones: the Weight column is cut off at the screen edge ('We', '12 kg' split), and the only cue that it scrolls is a faint shade. Meanwhile short cells wrap word by word ('About / 2 / years'), which makes rows three lines tall even though the table already scrolls.
findings.reference: The competitor shows nothing cut off at the edge on phones; any content that runs sideways shows a clear cue that it moves.
findings.fix: For .table-block__scroll[data-scroll="sideways"] th/td set white-space: nowrap so the cells keep their short values on one line, and give the scroll edge a stronger hint (a wider, darker fade on the right edge). Better still, tighten the cell padding at ≤600px so the four columns fit 350 px without scrolling.

findings.issue: At 1440 px the 'What this means for you' column runs across the whole content width, about 170 characters a line, which is too long to read comfortably.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps body text to a short measure (16–17px text in columns of roughly 60–75 characters, e.g. the two-column heading + text intro).
findings.fix: In reference.css cap the text cells' measure, e.g. .table-block td:last-child { max-inline-size: 75ch } with the table at inline-size: auto / max-content up to the content width, so the measure follows the copy rather than the full container.

findings.issue: The m5 heading ('Toddler Sizes and Custom Size Runs') is set in a regular weight, while table-1's heading on the same board and the site's h2 (DM Sans 700) are bold, so the two table modules carry headings of the same level in different weights (same at 390 px).
findings.reference: The competitor sets every section h2 in a heavy weight (Maison Neue 700–800) throughout.
findings.fix: Give the table module's heading (.table-block h2 / its intro heading) the site h2 weight, font-weight: 700, without touching its fitted size.

findings.issue: In both samples the quote button sits in a separate right-hand column, level with the paragraph's middle, instead of under the text it ends, which breaks the rule that a button stays in its copy's flow.
findings.reference: The competitor's inline CTA (product_manufacturer 13) sets heading, subtitle and paragraphs first, then its buttons on their own row directly below the copy.
findings.fix: In template.css, stop .cta (and .cta__content) from placing the actions beside the copy on wide screens: make the CTA a single column (e.g. flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start, or give the actions flex-basis: 100%) so the button starts on the content's left edge under the paragraph.

findings.issue: On phones the button runs the full column width with a large label that wraps onto two lines ('Request a quote for one-piece / swimsuits'), so it reads as a heavy block rather than a button.
findings.reference: The competitor's CTA buttons are compact black buttons sized to their one-line labels, in a smaller UI type than the body text.
findings.fix: In reference.css under max-width: 767px, size .block--cta[data-variant="inline"] .button--primary to its content (width: auto; justify-self/align-self: start) with a smaller label size and padding, so the label stays on one line where it fits and the button sits left-aligned under the text.

findings.issue: Step titles ('Enquiry and quotation', 'Sampling and fees', 'Send your first-run plan') are still set in regular weight at about the step text's size, so each column reads as two body paragraphs under its number circle with no title between them (the earlier finding, not yet fixed).
findings.reference: The competitor's step, card and sub-section titles are bold (Maison 700, e.g. card titles 700 22px), clearly heavier than their body copy.
findings.fix: In reference.css, next to `.block--process { --size-subheading: 1.0625rem; }`, set the step title's weight only, e.g. `.block--process .process-step__title { font-weight: 700; }`. Leave the size with the template.

findings.issue: On phones every step title ('Enquiry and quotation' … 'Branding and printing', 'Send your first-run plan') is the same size and weight as the 16px text under it, so the six stacked steps run together as plain paragraphs between the circles.
findings.reference: The competitor sets its step and card titles bold (700), apart from their text.
findings.fix: The same weight-only rule in reference.css: `.block--process .process-step__title { font-weight: 700; }`.

findings.issue: In the six-step sample, the hairline linking the circles runs only along the first row (01–03) and on past circle 03 to the content's right edge. The second row's circles (04–06) stand without it, so the two rows of one sequence look like two different treatments.
findings.reference: The competitor's step rows (the six-step timeline on navy) draw one continuous hairline across every step of the row it belongs to, and it ends with the last step.
findings.fix: In the shared process:circles CSS, draw the connector per step (e.g. a `::after` line on each step's marker running to the next marker in the same row, left off the last step of each row) instead of one line on the list's first row.

findings.issue: The fabric comparison table in the tinted panel has opaque white fades over its left edge (the empty top-left header cell) and right edge (the 'Branded or recycled fabric' column) although the table fits its box, so white smears show on the beige panel at both widths (the end of 'Higher' and 'Hero styles' fades out on mobile).
findings.reference: The competitor's proof/text modules are plain text on the section's own background, with no scroll shades or patches of another colour.
findings.fix: In patterns.css (ProseBlock.astro / ArticleChart.astro), set data-scroll="sideways" only when the table is wider than its box (scrollWidth > clientWidth, measured again on resize). Paint the `local` cover gradients in the background of the box the table sits in (e.g. a --table-scroll-cover variable that defaults to the section or panel surface) instead of a fixed var(--surface-primary).

findings.issue: Every cell of the comparison table is ruled with a 1px black border (--border-color #000) on all four sides, a heavy full grid that reads darker than anything else in the section.
findings.reference: The competitor's proof modules use no borders at all: light text blocks in Maison Book with only an underlined link as accent; our own table-block uses only thin row rules.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set `.block--proof .prose__table :is(th, td)` (or the section-charts table) to `border: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid` a light rule colour (e.g. --border-table / #e5e5e5), and keep a slightly heavier bottom rule only under the header row.

findings.issue: At 390px the three-column table inside the padded tinted panel squeezes each cell to one or two words a line (e.g. 'LYCRA Xtra / Life, / Carvico, / ECONYL, / REPREVE', 'Branded or / recycled / fabric'), so each row runs four to five lines high.
findings.reference: The competitor's proof text runs the full content width on phones with no inset panel.
findings.fix: In reference.css, reduce the tinted panel's inline padding and the cell padding of `.prose__table th, td` under 600px (e.g. 0.5rem) so the columns get the width back.

findings.issue: The step titles ('Rinse in fresh water', 'Wash cold, inside out', 'Dry flat in shade') are set at weight 600, lighter than the competitor's card titles, so they barely stand out from the 1rem body text under them.
findings.reference: The competitor's outlined cards set their title in Maison 700 (22px/33px) with the text below, so the title clearly outweighs the body.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set font-weight: 700 on .block--process[data-variant="photo-cards"] .process-step h3, overriding the template's 600. Leave its size to the template.

findings.issue: The cards have only about 20px of side padding (1.25rem), so titles and text sit tight against the white outline. With the generous top padding under the number badge, this makes the cards look cramped at the sides.
findings.reference: The competitor's outlined cards use about 32.66px of padding on every side.
findings.fix: In reference.css, raise padding-inline on .block--process[data-variant="photo-cards"] .process-step to about 2rem.

findings.issue: On phones each card has about 45–55px of empty space under its last line, against about 36px above the title. The extra space seems to come from the paragraph's bottom margin plus the card's padding, which leaves every stacked card looking bottom-heavy.
findings.reference: The competitor's cards use the same padding on all sides, so the content sits evenly inside the outline.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set margin-bottom: 0 on .block--process[data-variant="photo-cards"] .process-step p:last-child, so the card's own padding is the only space under the text.

findings.issue: The band's button sits only a few pixels under the step-05 text ("and trimming.") and is pushed part-way across the section, neither on the content's left edge nor centred on it; the same happens in faq-steps, where it nearly touches step 02's "delivers within 6 to 8 weeks".
findings.reference: The competitor's band ends in its own row on the content's left edge, a clear gap below the steps (the closing line "From handover to delivery…"), never squeezed against one step's text.
findings.fix: In patterns.css, have .process__cta start on the content's left edge (justify-content: flex-start) on a full row after .process-steps (grid-column: 1 / -1 if it ends up inside a grid), with a top margin of at least the step grid's gap (e.g. margin-top: clamp(2rem, 4vw, 3rem)), so the button stays in the copy's flow under the steps.

findings.issue: On phones the full-width button sits right up against step 07's last line ("arranged by our in-house team."), with no gap between them.
findings.reference: The competitor leaves a clear gap between the last step and what closes the band.
findings.fix: The same .process__cta change in patterns.css: a margin-top at least the step gap, so the button stands apart from the last step.

findings.issue: The step titles ("Consultation and design", "Tech pack and patterns", …) are set in regular weight at nearly body size, so they do not stand out from the step text under them.
findings.reference: The competitor sets each step name ("Fabrics & Colours", "Handover", "Costing") bold, clearly heavier than its description.
findings.fix: In reference.css, give .block--process[data-variant="band"] .process-step__title font-weight: 700, keeping its size from the template (--size-subheading, which is already larger than the body text).

findings.issue: On phones each step number ("01", "02"…) is indented from the text's left edge and stands in a tall empty box, so the stacked list has large uneven gaps between number, title and text and runs very long (about 900 px for five one-line steps).
findings.reference: The competitor's step number is a small label flush with its title's left edge, directly above it.
findings.fix: In reference.css, size the band's marker to its text: .block--process[data-variant="band"] .process-step__marker { width: auto; height: auto; place-items: start; } so the number sits on the left edge and the step's 0.75rem gap applies.

findings.issue: The step numbers are white like the body text, and the 44 px circle around them indents them past the column's edge, so the numbering does not read as an accent.
findings.reference: The competitor sets its step numbers ("01"–"06") small, bold and in its light-blue accent, flush left above each step name.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set --process-marker-text on .block--process[data-variant="band"] to the light accent (the button's cyan) and size the marker to its text (width/height: auto, place-items: start).

findings.issue: The band has no heading: it opens with a body-size lead ("Our full-package service, from brief to shipment.") straight above the steps, so the section has no title.
findings.reference: The competitor's band opens with an eyebrow ("HOW IT WORKS") and a large H2 ("Six steps from Costing to delivery") above a rule.
findings.fix: Site Factory should give this process block a heading (e.g. "Seven Steps from Brief to Shipment") so it renders h2.process__heading above the lead.

findings.issue: The band has neither a heading nor a lead: five bare steps start straight under the section's top padding, so the dark band has no visible purpose.
findings.reference: The competitor's band always opens with an eyebrow and an H2 naming the process.
findings.fix: Site Factory should give faq-steps a heading (e.g. "How a Consulting Project Runs") and, if it has one, a short lead.

findings.issue: The heading 'A recent order' starts on the content's left edge, but the case cards below it are a 46rem stack centred in the column, so they start about 330px to the right of the heading and leave an empty band on the left at both copy lengths.
findings.reference: The competitor sets each section's heading, text and cards in one shared column from the same left edge. Its sections never pair a left-set heading with a centred block of content.
findings.fix: In src/styles/patterns.css, change `.order-cases` (max-width: 46rem; margin-inline: auto) so the stack starts on the heading's edge. Use `margin-inline: 0` when body[data-heading-align="start"] is set, keeping max-width as the measure limit. Alternatively, let the stack fill the content width as an equal-grid that puts the cards side by side when there are several.

findings.issue: The same three-word heading 'A recent order' is rendered at two clearly different sizes: about 60px in the longest sample and about 40px in the shortest. The same words in the same module should fit to the same size.
findings.reference: The competitor uses one size for each heading level in every section (60/60 desktop section headings).
findings.fix: Make the template's heading-fit for `.order-case__heading` depend only on the heading's own words, so it returns the same size for identical headings whatever the length of the block's body copy. Change only the fit logic, not a font-size rule.

findings.issue: Every bar starts closed and the answer style never shows, while this site's FAQ setting for opening the first answer applies to the whole site (it is set to closed for the home FAQ).
findings.reference: The competitor's solution FAQ bars open the first question ("Do I need a tech pack?"), so its answer copy shows under the bold question in the white bar.
findings.fix: Let the template set the first-answer-open choice per variant or page type, so faq:bars opens its first item while the home two-column FAQ stays closed.

findings.issue: The open/close mark is a + at the right end of each bar, while the bars variant's mark sits at the left of the question.
findings.reference: The competitor puts a small solid triangle (▸, turning ▾ when open) just before the question text, at the left of each bar.
findings.fix: Give faq[data-variant="bars"] a marker option in the template that puts a triangle before the summary text, instead of the shared ::after + at the right.

findings.issue: The comparison table under the shortest FAQ draws a full dark 1px grid around every cell, which the competitor's light FAQ module never uses. A white fade sits over its empty top-left cell and its right edge, although the table fits the width without scrolling.
findings.reference: The competitor's FAQ module uses no heavy rules: white bars on a cream band, the only edges being the bars' own soft rounded corners.
findings.fix: Change the table's cell borders in .block--charts (or the table rule in reference.css) to hairline rows only (border-color mixed to about 18% of the text colour, no vertical rules), and show the scroll fade only when the table really overflows.

findings.issue: On phones the table shows only three of its four columns, with headers broken onto three lines. The fade sits at the left of the first column instead of the right edge where the hidden "Pigment with white underlayer" column is, so nothing tells the reader to swipe.
findings.reference: The competitor's FAQ has no table. Its phone layout keeps one bar per question with short readable lines.
findings.fix: Put the overflow fade (or a 'swipe' cue) on the right edge while more columns are hidden, or stack the table into one card per column below about 600px.

findings.issue: On phones each bar's track takes only about half the panel width, and its value ("4 cm", "7 cm") is pushed to the far right, leaving an empty gap between bar and figure.
findings.reference: On desktop the same chart lets the track run the width between label and value, with the value right after it.
findings.fix: On narrow widths, let .charts bar tracks grow (flex: 1) to fill the row up to the value, so bar and figure keep together.

findings.issue: The photo's top edge doesn't line up with the form's. The heading 'Send an enquiry' sits in the photo column only, which pushes the photo down by about the heading's height, while the Name/Email fields start level with the heading.
findings.reference: The competitor puts a heading over each column ('Have Questions?' / 'Email Us'), so the photo and the first form row start on the same line.
findings.fix: In the form:media layout, put the section heading in a row above both columns (or start the form column under the heading too), so that .form-block__media and .form-block__form share their top edge.

findings.issue: The consent line reads '…as described in the privacy policy. Privacy policy': LeadForm.astro adds a separate 'Privacy policy' link after a label that already ends with those words.
findings.reference: The competitor's form has no repeated text under its fields; its only element below the message box is the button.
findings.fix: In LeadForm.astro, turn the words 'privacy policy' inside consent.label into the link instead of appending a second 'Privacy policy' link after the label.

findings.issue: The submit button is a short pill at the form's left edge, while every field above it spans the whole form column.
findings.reference: The competitor's SEND button runs the full width of the form column, level with the fields above it.
findings.fix: In reference.css, add width: 100% to :is(.form-block__form, .cta__form) .button--primary. The button stays where it is in the form, under the consent line.

findings.issue: reference.css sets the submit button to min-height 37px, which is below the 44px minimum tap target on phones.
findings.reference: The competitor's button is a slim dark bar sized for desktop; on a phone that height is too small to tap reliably.
findings.fix: In reference.css, inside @media (max-width: 767px), raise :is(.form-block__form, .cta__form) .button--primary to min-height: 44px and keep the dark #262626 look.

findings.issue: On phones the four channel cards stack one per row at full width, so each card is about 230 px tall and the section runs to about 1030 px, mostly empty card space around one icon, one label bar and one line of text.
findings.reference: The competitor's channel cards go two by two on phones (components.md, contact section 3): small outlined tiles, each with an icon above a black label bar.
findings.fix: In patterns.css, change `@media (max-width: 599px) .contact-channels[data-variant="cards"] > .contact-channel { flex-basis: 100% }` to two columns (flex-basis: calc(50% - var(--grid-gap) / 2)) so the four cards sit two by two.

findings.issue: The 'Contact details' heading starts on the content's left edge, but the row of four cards is centred under it (from about x≈850 to 1360 on the shot), so the heading stands alone at the left and does not line up with the cards.
findings.reference: On the competitor's page the heading and cards share one axis (the heading is centred there). Our rule keeps the heading at the left edge, so the card set has to start under it. Only a grid's own short last row is centred.
findings.fix: In patterns.css, set .contact-channels[data-variant="cards"] to justify-content: flex-start, or make it a grid of equal 1fr columns across the content width, so the first card starts under the heading's left edge. A short last row can still be centred.

findings.issue: The cards keep a fixed 245 px width taken from the competitor (--channel-card-width: 15.3125rem). This leaves most of the row empty and squeezes the Hours text, so '9:00-18:00' breaks after the hyphen into '9:00-' / '18:00'.
findings.reference: The competitor's cards are sized to its own short labels. Our copy is longer (an email address, a two-line address, opening hours), so the card width should follow our copy, not a copied fixed value.
findings.fix: In reference.css, drop --channel-card-width so the cards share the content width. Also keep the time range on one line (white-space: nowrap on the time span, or a non-breaking en dash in the copy).

findings.issue: The cards start right under the 'Contact details' heading with no gap; the card borders touch the heading's descenders. Phones show the same.
findings.reference: The competitor leaves clear space between a section's heading and its content.
findings.fix: In reference.css, add space above the card list (for example .contact-channels[data-variant="cards"] { margin-block-start: var(--space-md) }) so the heading and cards keep the site's usual heading-to-content gap.
